references.text: Parallel structure where a recipient of kindness requests a binding oath for mutual protection of the family.
Theological connection between Abraham's status as a foreigner and God's promise of the land to his descendants.
Repetition of the motif of 'kindness and faithfulness' (hesed) as the basis for covenants in Abraham's story.
Theological contrast between the oath's role as a necessary guarantee in the OT and the warning against oaths in the NT.
The principle of mutual 'hesed' (kindness) as the foundation for peace between former adversaries.
Direct parallel in structure and content: prayer for an oath not to destroy descendants.
Complementary aspects of Abraham's offspring: prophetic dominion (Gen 27:29) and diplomatic peace (Gen 21:23).
Context in Abraham's story: God's oath to Abraham (Gen 24:7) as the basis for his diplomatic position (Gen 21:23).
Narrative parallel: Abraham's and Isaac's covenants with Philistine kings regarding non-aggression based on mutual kindness.
